summary: Discovery + POC scoping focused on Argentum Mobility's conversational routing assistant. Goal: define workload signature (QPS, concurrency, token distribution), success criteria (95th pct latency, accuracy regression bounds), and benchmark plan to decide Hosted vs Dedicated. Redwood AE/SE outlined telemetry needs, suggested staged pilot and A/B fallbacks and discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs.
topics: timeline and infra requirements for pilot
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-04-07 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Emma Carter, Miguel Santos - Redwood; Priya Nair, Daniel Cho, Anita Gomez, Samir Patel - Argentum Mobility

Auto-summary: quick POC scope, baseline telemetry ask, agree pilot week and deliverables

00:00 Emma Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm emma carter, AE at Redwood Inference. Miguel and i will run through what we need to size a POC. can folks introduce themselves quick?
00:12 Priya Nair: yeah hi i'm priya, lead ml eng for the routing assistant. we handle intent classification and downstream triage to human ops. we've been tracking latency and costs per request.
00:22 Daniel Cho: daniel, platform engineer. i'll be the person who helps hook up the test env, VPC peering and egress.
:28 Anita Gomez: Anita, product, i'll be tracking success criteria and customer impact.
00:31 Emma Carter: great. high-level — goal here is to create a reproducible benchmark so by the end of the pilot you can choose hosted api or dedicated reserved capacity with clear cost/latency numbers. key things we need: QPS profile (peak and sustained), concurrency, prompt token dist., and a set of target SLAs.
00:50 Priya Nair: on qps, production today sees big spikes at 8am and 5pm local — baseline is ~12 RPS sustained and spikes to 220 RPS rare events, about 15% of traffic. median request 50 input tokens / 80 output tokens but for some flows output is 300 tokens.
01:10 Miguel Santos: okay that's useful. so we need token mix breakdown: percent of short (<32), medium (32-128), long (>128) inputs and outputs. also, do you use KV cache across the conversational turns? that impacts memory and reuse.
01:25 Priya Nair: yes we hold per-session context, average session length 5 turns. I think kv cache hit is high for the same session but very low across different users.
01:36 Daniel Cho: from infra side, we have strict egress rules and SSO via Okta, SOC2 cert in progress. Any privacy constraints?
01:45 Anita Gomez: we need data residency within EU for some subset of customers, and we cannot send PII off-prem for certain contracts.
01:53 Emma Carter: understood. for the pilot we can run in a private VPC in eu-west or use a staging hosted cluster with regional routing. we'll note the PII constraints — for benchmarking we only need anonymized telemetry.
02:05 Miguel Santos: quick note on measurement: our suggestion is to capture tail latencies (p50/p90/p95/p99), token-level cost estimate, model quality delta on a labeled eval set, and failure rates (timeouts, OOMs). The benchmark harness we'll share simulates the mix of prompt lengths and session stickiness.
02:28 Priya Nair: about success criteria, product cares about: 95th pct latency < 350ms for short responses, for long generations it's okay up to 900ms but we care about p99 < 2.5s. Also cost per 10k requests should be under our current vendor spend, we'll share numbers.
02:50 Emma Carter: good — we'll include those as hard targets. in many cases for your 220 rps spikes we recommend burst capacity and can show a cost delta between dedicated and hosted for sustained vs spiky loads.
03:05 Miguel Santos: on modeling concurrency — two approaches: constant concurrency per-GPU or multiplexed batching. given your mixture we'll probably recommend dynamic batching with a max token cap and session-aware batching so KV caches are preserved where helpful.
03:25 Daniel Cho: can you explain the session-aware batching bit?
03:28 Miguel Santos: sure — so we group requests that share similar token lengths and priorities while keeping requests from same session routed to the same worker so cache hits remain. there's a tradeoff: higher cache hits lowers compute per token, but shard affinity can reduce batching headroom.
03:46 Priya Nair: makes sense. what about quantization? we've tested int8 briefly.
03:50 Emma Carter: Redwood supports quantized variants in the catalog; we recommend validating quality on your eval set. we'll include quantization profiles in the benchmark matrix (float16, int8 sims).
04:02 Anita Gomez: what's the minimal telemetry you need? we need to minimize PII exposure.
04:06 Emma Carter: anonymized request metadata: timestamp, prompt token count, response token count, session id hashed, route id, latency, error code. no raw prompts unless you want us to sign an NDA, but top-50 prompt patterns as examples are helpful.
04:25 Priya Nair: we'll provide the telemetry and top prompts. expectation to complete that by Apr 14.
04:30 Miguel Santos: benchmark plan outline: stage 1 - offline simulation with replayed telemetry to measure expected cost and average latency; stage 2 - small pilot on a dedicated test cluster to measure tail latency and model correctness; stage 3 - extended pilot under realistic spikes and failover tests.
04:55 Daniel Cho: how long will each stage take?
04:58 Emma Carter: stage 1 - 3 business days once we have telemetry; stage 2 - 4 business days to run and analyze; stage 3 - 5-7 business days for extended stress and fallbacks. so overall 3 weeks approx.
05:15 Priya Nair: timeline is tight but okay, we want decision before end of May to line up budget.
05:20 Emma Carter: that's doable. we'll aim to deliver results by May 20.
05:28 Miguel Santos: for load generation we'll share JMeter/Locust scripts and a lightweight injector that respects session stickiness and token distribution. we'll also set up metrics dashboards for token-level cost and per-route latency.
05:43 Anita Gomez: any security docs we should expect?
05:45 Emma Carter: yes — SOC2, ISO attestation, network diagrams, and an architecture note for private deployments. i'll attach them.
05:58 Priya Nair: about SLA — we're looking for 99.9% availability and predictable tail latency, but for pilot we'll accept lower. can you do regional fallbacks if eu-west saturates?
06:12 Miguel Santos: yes, routing policies can fallback to another region or to a cheaper model variant. we'll show the automated fallback configuration in the pilot.
06:25 Samir Patel (CTO): one question — if we go dedicated, how does autoscaling handle burst 10x spikes?
06:33 Emma Carter: dedicated has reserved capacity plus burst buckets; autoscaling config allows headroom and can route overflow to hosted pools with cost differential. we'll model cost for both.
06:45 Priya Nair: for metrics, we also want token-level breakdown per intent; we'll map the top 10 intents to token profiles.
06:53 Miguel Santos: perfect. that's useful for model selection — some intents prefer shorter outputs which can be routed to cheaper quantized variants.
07:05 Emma Carter: ok let's recap next steps before close.
07:09 Emma Carter: Redwood: share benchmark plan + scripts (Emma), quantization profile recommendations (Miguel). Arg: provide anonymized telemetry and top-50 prompts (Priya), set up peering/rules (Daniel). schedule pilot week Apr 26.
07:28 Priya Nair: yes we'll aim for those dates. thanks everyone.
07:33 Emma Carter: great thanks all, i'll follow up with calendar invite and the docs. bye.

Notes: occasional transcription errors — e.g., "K-V cash" appears instead of KV cache, "p99 top" as p99; some names misattributed in mid-section. Links referenced: https://redwood.example.com/benchmark-plan (sample), spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/benchmark-argentum (access upon request).
